Stock AUTOMAPS.DAT has 17 non-0xFF bytes: cells (6..10,5) and column 8 rows 6..13 plus (9,11) = the walk north from the start cell (8,13) (matches LastPosition 0xD8), and three plane-B bytes at B[60],B[76],B[92].

invariants: Write CAWCHAR.DAT with the cipher  (for bytes 8..0x1CB of each slot). There is no checksum anywhere (the cipher is a bijection over the 0x1C4 bytes; both programs decode any bytes).
RUINS rejects a slot unless rec[0x17D]==rec[0x1AB] and the value is 3 (4 = "off-line character above level 20", RUINS exits). TWGENN does not check it. A new character gets 3 in both.
Name appears three places: rec+0x08 (gallery list), rec+0xE7 (what the game loads as the in-game name). Keep both equal, NUL-padded to 10 bytes; epithet rec+0x13.
SelectedSlot header byte must index an occupied slot (header[1+slot]==1) else the gallery shows Vacant.

RUINS and TWGENN clamp, not reject: Strength 0..99, Defense (RUINS: >115 becomes 99), Agility and Initiative 0..50, Dexterity 0..3200, MaxHealth and MaxMana 0..32000, spell and skill ranks 0..12 (clamp routine RUINS 20F2:00A5 = TWGENN 18B3:00D6). Current health is also clamped to 32000 in the RUINS main loop. Exceeding these gets silently reduced the next time the clamp runs.
Load clears status: mem+0x16, mem+0x34, player obj+0x23/+0x25 are zeroed on every load.
CurrentHealth/CurrentMana are separate words from MaxHealth/MaxMana; keep current <= max.
AUTOMAPS.DAT has no header and no checksum; the 800-byte block of a map can be edited freely. 0xFF means unexplored.

CHARKEY.DAT is never read for validation: TWGENN (0498) and RUINS (11E2:000C -> 1200:0275) only APPEND the four key words as decimal text (fprintf "%d%d%d%d" = "11033160152404102") when running on-line; the read-back-and-compare routines (TWGENN 04F9, RUINS 1200:02D2) have no callers. The file is not consulted when loading CAWCHAR.DAT.
MAXSTAT.DAT/.ROT and RACEDEFS.DAT/.CAW are not opened by RUINS.EXE or TWGENN.EXE (no file name string in either exe or any RESOURCE file); they cannot affect an edited character in the client.
